svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cut 498 mm of 40 x 40 x 2 tube; square both ends (the pole end

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: must sit flat on the plate) and deburr.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Plate end: two 6.6 mm holes straight through top and bottom walls,

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: on the centre line, 15 and 30 mm from the end.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Head end: two 5.5 mm holes straight through, on the centre line,

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 418 and 478 mm from the plate end.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Drill each pair square through both walls (drill press, V-block).

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cut four crush spacers 36 mm long from 10 mm aluminium tube; they

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: sit inside the tube on the bolts so the walls do not crush.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fit a plastic end cap in the head end.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check: on a flat bench the tube does not rock; holes line up

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: top to bottom (a rod passes straight through).
